tools.name: submit_scrape
tools.description: Submit a scrape job. Optionally pass table_id from get_tables to add results to an existing writable static Table; omit it to keep results in All leads only. Paid scrapers spend vendor credits (BYOK) or lead credits (managed: 1 credit per NEW lead, deduped free), so confirm paid work with the user first. For every paid scraper, pass a positive hard_max_cost_usd equal to or above the estimate after the user confirms that ceiling; paid work will not start without it. A scraper with requires_credential=false is free and needs no integration_id, credential_id, or hard maximum. billing: "auto" (default) uses the workspace key when one exists, else Scrapeloop's managed key; "byok"/"managed" force the mode. integration_id is required for normal BYOK, optional for managed, and omitted for credential-free sources. Returns 402 for budget or credit limits and 409 when rescrape confirmation is needed; pass confirm_rescrape:true to proceed past a coverage conflict. Retry contract: Durable Idempotency-Key required. Transient retries replay one stored result.

tools.description: Preview all-now or over-time scraping with the same limits as the app. Native coverage_mode complete previews up to 100000 frozen searches as a draft with no raw-row caps; output and cost remain unknown until measured. No scrape or credential is created. Read the Playbook and scraper capabilities first. Set a lead or credit cap for credit-priced work, or a dollar cap for dollar-priced work. all_now limits apply once; over_time limits reset each month. Show costs and coverage warnings before creating. Retry contract: Read-only operation. Retries transport errors, 429, and 5xx with bounded backoff.

tools.name: create_scrape_plan
tools.description: Save a scrape plan into an existing writable Table. Native coverage_mode complete requires start_mode draft, a stable scope_operation_id and no monthly raw-row caps. Optional rescrape_after_days waits until the full pass finishes, then waits the saved delay; old journals and monthly credit limits are preserved. It saves the whole scope in restartable batches and requires saved shared budgets and the exact complete-plan launch review before Start. Set start_mode to draft to save without starting searches or spending. The default active mode starts approved work and can spend credits or vendor money. Preview the exact choices first and stay within the approved limit and time period. Pass explicit territory values and matching billing limits. Reuse the same idempotency_key after a lost reply, inspect list_scrape_plans and never create a second plan to escape an uncertain result. Over-time limits reset monthly; a total one-time approval does not authorize recurring spend. Retry contract: Durable Idempotency-Key required. Transient retries replay one stored result.

tools.name: get_scrape_plan_ready_goal

Retries transport errors, 429, and 5xx with bounded backoff.

tools.name: get_scrape_plan_yield

This is not a national accuracy claim, cost quote or spending approval. Retry contract: Read-only operation. Retries transport errors, 429, and 5xx with bounded backoff.

tools.name: set_scrape_plan_ready_goal
tools.description: Save a verified-email goal on a native Maps draft with optional whole-scope repeat searches after the saved delay. Choose the ready Table and its email campaign, monthly goal/minimum, optional hard-maximum mode, unused-stock ceiling and evidence rules. supply_mode on_demand searches only while the linked campaign has room (plus buffer_days of its daily intake); only then may monthly_goal be null, with limit_mode target and monthly_minimum 0. allow_role counts an exact Role result (info@, office@) as ready and allow_resolved_catchall counts a catch-all that passed the second check: both must match the Table rules and the campaign, which check_campaign_setup verifies. Always send monthly_minimum and timezone: their defaults suit one business only. Pass the reviewed expected_updated_at from get_scrape_plan. Counts require current input-bound verification, qualification, campaign fields and sender-history checks. This does not start scraping, verification or campaigns. Complete-search pacing must be available before Start. Retry contract: One request only. An ambiguous result returns reconciliation tools and stable match fields.

tools.name: get_scrape_plan_budget
tools.description: Read shared monthly and lifetime lead/verify credit limits, reserved work and remaining allowance. Open holds stay counted across month changes. This makes no provider calls. Retry contract: Read-only operation. Retries transport errors, 429, and 5xx with bounded backoff.

tools.name: set_scrape_plan_budget
tools.description: Save reviewed credit limits and Table ownership for a paused complete-search plan with a ready-email goal. All four credit answers are required. A number is a limit; explicit null means no plan limit for that one (then only the workspace balance stops the plan), and omission is rejected. Zero blocks spending. No-cap checks still require allowed tools, bounded jobs and available workspace credits. Never infer no cap without approval. Include Raw, Email ready and every check Table. One Table belongs to one budget. Preserve expected_revision from the current budget; omit it only for the first save. A lost reply requires readback before retry. This starts no work and does not enable checks. website_language permits the free bounded Website languages preset with a saved attempt. owner_website explicitly permits the free bounded system Owner name finder; it still needs a saved job and attempt. review_history permits only the system Google review stats preset with source explicitly outscraper and a separate review_budget in USD, default zero. Select an existing connection from get_scrape_plan_budget.review_connections. Omitted review_budget preserves saved settings. Each row reserves 0.147 USD; recorded units use the published ceiling, not a confirmed account invoice. Unknown requests stay held and never retry. business_email_finder permits a Business email finder column that was made with confirmed_only on (create_table_native_column options). Such a column keeps only an address the email check called real, holds 3 verify credits per row and charges 1 per check that got an answer. A Business email finder column without confirmed_only stays blocked, because it can keep an address nobody confirmed. Google-first, custom recipes and other paid vendors remain blocked. Use review_complete_scrape_plan to check readiness before requesting exact launch approval. Retry contract: One request only. An ambiguous result returns reconciliation tools and stable match fields.

tools.name: set_scrape_plan_supply
tools.description: Change when a paused complete plan searches, and whether it counts role addresses. supply_mode monthly works toward monthly_goal; on_demand searches only while the linked campaign has room plus buffer_days of its daily intake. monthly_goal null (no monthly ready-lead limit) is allowed only with on_demand, limit_mode target and monthly_minimum 0. allow_role true counts an exact Role result (info@, office@) as ready; omit it to keep the saved choice. Always send buffer_days and monthly_minimum: left out, they are reset to 3 and 0. The scope, ready count, campaign and credit limits stay. Pass expected_updated_at from get_scrape_plan read after the pause. The plan then needs review_complete_scrape_plan and launch_complete_scrape_plan again. This starts no search. Retry contract: One request only. An ambiguous result returns reconciliation tools and stable match fields.

tools.name: switch_scrape_plan_campaign
tools.description: Point a paused complete plan at another email campaign that reads the same ready Table. The plan must be paused by a person, both campaigns must have filling off, the new campaign must be an open Instantly campaign, and no check or Table move may be running (otherwise 409: wait and try again). The ready count, the searches done and the credit limits stay. Afterwards switch filling on for the new campaign, then review and launch the plan again. This uploads nothing and starts no search. Retry contract: One request only. An ambiguous result returns reconciliation tools and stable match fields.

tools.name: update_scrape_plan
tools.description: Switch Google review counting on or off for the next searches of a Scrapeloop Maps plan. Needed when a Table rule asks for the review count. The plan must be paused, and a complete plan must have no place half searched. A complete plan then needs review_complete_scrape_plan and launch_complete_scrape_plan again. Limits and search area are not changed by this tool. Retry contract: Proven idempotent write. Retries transient failures with bounded backoff.

tools.name: check_campaign_setup
tools.description: One free read that walks a whole self-filling campaign and says whether its parts fit each other: the search plan, the Tables and rules on the way, the checks, the email answer (Table rule, plan goal and campaign must agree), the campaign, the credit limits and the approval. Pass plan_id for a search plan, or campaign_id to start from a campaign (works with no plan too). Returns fits (true only when nothing is fail and nothing is unknown), counts, and checks in the order a lead travels; each has step, key, status (ok, warn, fail or unknown), a plain title and detail, and often fixes: the exact tool and args that end it. Run it after every build step and before asking for a start. Apply a fix only as its note says, ask the person before any fix that changes who gets an email or what may be spent, and run this again afterwards. It changes nothing, starts nothing and approves nothing. deep=false is the quick check: it skips the sender read, the Start check of the campaign and the count of leads that meet a rule and have not moved, so it can say fits while one of those three would not. Use the full check before a start. Retry contract: Read-only operation. Retries transport errors, 429, and 5xx with bounded backoff.

tools.name: review_complete_scrape_plan
tools.description: Read the exact complete-search scope, ready-output goal, Table rules, shared limits, repeat delay and current launch blockers. Free read. This does not start source work, checks or campaigns. Retry contract: Read-only operation. Retries transport errors, 429, and 5xx with bounded backoff.

tools.name: launch_complete_scrape_plan
tools.description: Start or resume a complete native search after explicit approval of the exact reviewed plan, enabled checks and monthly/full-plan limits. This can spend credits. Requires the snapshot hash and updated timestamp from review_complete_scrape_plan, plus one stable operation UUID. A changed plan needs a fresh review. After uncertainty, read the plan and review; preserve the same operation and body. Never use this for sender Start or GHL writes. Retry contract: One request only. An ambiguous result returns reconciliation tools and stable match fields.

tools.name: check_scrape_plan_stop
tools.description: Look at the stop a complete search plan is on. Use it when get_scrape_plan shows the block "A check is on hold", "Search needs review" or "A lead could not be moved between Tables". Also use it when the block is "You paused it" and its words say that something of the plan is on hold: such a plan cannot start again until that is cleared, and it stays paused after. With dry_run true (the default) it only reads saved records. It says what it found and what would happen, with the credits that could use, and it returns job_ids: the ids of the held jobs and failed moves it looked at. To carry on, call it again with dry_run false and those same job_ids. It then acts only where the records prove that is safe. A held Table check: it ends the held job, gives unused held check credits back, runs free checks that never finished again, and runs paid checks that never started inside the plan limits, unless a person pressed Stop on the Table: then those stay closed. A paid check that got no answer is closed and never asked again. It sends no request to a checker itself. A held map search: it puts the same search back in the queue with its same held lead credits. At most one map square that got no answer is searched again, in at most 2 extra rounds per square (the app tries a square up to 3 times in one round). A review count read that got no answer is closed and never asked again. A plan that a person paused stays paused: the search only finishes what it already read. A failed Table move: it only marks the move done when the lead is already in the Table it had to go to. It never moves a lead. The answer has outcome safe, needs_person, wait or nothing, with a title, plain lines and a next line, all ready to show the person. Always show the dry run lines first and carry on only after the person says yes. If the stops changed since the dry run, nothing is changed and a fresh dry run comes back with changed true. A second call after it carried on finds nothing on hold. Retry contract: Proven idempotent write. Retries transient failures with bounded backoff.

tools.name: pause_scrape_plan
tools.description: Pause new work from a scrape plan. A job already running may still finish. Inspect the plan and its jobs after pausing. Retry contract: Never retried automatically. An ambiguous result must be reconciled before any new attempt.

tools.description: Start a saved draft after reviewing its scope, destination and cost limits with the user. This can spend credits or vendor money. Requires approval for the exact plan and budget. Pass expected_updated_at from the reviewed get_scrape_plan response. Changed drafts must be reviewed again. After a lost reply inspect get_scrape_plan; never retry blindly. Retry contract: Never retried automatically. An ambiguous result must be reconciled before any new attempt.

tools.name: get_job

A scrape job carries `delivery`: how many rows were found, kept, new, already yours, and added to its Table, why rows were left out, and whether adding them to the Table worked. New native Maps receipts also include search_coverage: complete, partial, or missing proof. Job completion alone never proves a whole place was covered. Retry contract: Read-only operation. Retries transport errors, 429, and 5xx with bounded backoff.

tools.name: cancel_job

An active external vendor task remains nonterminal while the worker aborts it and settles final partial usage, then becomes cancelled. Retry contract: Never retried automatically. An ambiguous result must be reconciled before any new attempt.

tools.name: attach_job_to_table

Use it only when get_job shows `delivery.attach.state` as "failed" and the job is done, and not when `delivery.attach.code` is "table_missing" (that Table was deleted). Rows already in the Table are skipped, so repeating it never adds a row twice. Returns `added`, `in_table`, and the updated `delivery`. Retry contract: Proven idempotent write. Retries transient failures with bounded backoff.

tools.name: search_leads

Pass a filters object (job_titles_include, job_titles_mode: "contains" (default) | "exact" | "similar", seniorities, functions, countries, states, cities, company_keywords_include, company_names, domains_include, industries, decision_maker, email_quality_labels, ...). Industries are coarse inferred sector buckets from the company name, not verified firmographics. Company size and revenue filters (employee_ranges, revenue_ranges, and related fields) are deprecated no-ops; fold size hints into company_keywords_include. Get valid slugs from get_meta("industries"). Free, costs no credits. Retry contract: Read-only operation. Retries transport errors, 429, and 5xx with bounded backoff.

tools.name: create_table_native_column
tools.description: Attach one native Scrapeloop tool as a real Smart Table column: verify_email, verify_phone, email_finder, business_email_finder, linkedin_finder, linkedin_activity, google_profile. These are Scrapeloop's first-party tools, several of which superseded legacy presets, so they are addressed by tool key here rather than by preset slug through create_table_preset_column (which refuses a superseded slug for a new column). Each bills MANAGED VERIFICATION CREDITS per row, never dollars and never the customer's own vendor keys: verify_email reserves 1 credit per selected row, verify_phone reserves 5, each email finder reserves 3, linkedin_finder reserves 5, linkedin_activity reserves 3, and google_profile reserves 1. Settlement charges only fresh vendor checks and returns the unused reservation; missing inputs, cached rows, and skipped rows are free. linkedin_finder charges its 5 credits only for a row where it found the owner's LinkedIn profile; a row with no owner found is free. linkedin_activity reads each row's personal LinkedIn profile and newest post and labels it Active, Maybe or Weak (cell text), so LinkedIn invites go to people likely to answer; it charges 3 credits only for a profile it read, and rows with no personal profile, cached rows and profiles that no longer exist are free. google_profile finds a business on Google Maps for a lead that did not come from Google Maps (a Yelp lead, an imported list): it searches the business name in its town, accepts a result only when the phone, the website or the exact name in the same town matches, and saves place_id, gbp_url, rating and reviews_count on the cell (status found, not_found or unclear) and the place ID on a lead that had none; it charges 1 credit only for a profile found, and a business not on Google, more than one matching profile and cached rows are free. Filter on col.<key>.reviews_count to keep small businesses; a business with no reviews yet is saved as 0, and an unknown count has no number and never passes a numeric rule. Creating a column is always free. auto_run defaults false and queues nothing; when auto_run would backfill existing rows the API returns a 409 estimate whose cost.total_credits is the real charge, and you confirm it with confirm_auto_run plus confirmed_credits (CREDITS, not dollars - estimated_cost_usd is our vendor cost and is far smaller than what the workspace is billed). An auto_run that exceeds the workspace verify-credit balance returns 402 with {credit_kind, required, available} before anything is created. The Table master auto-run switch and workspace budget caps stay fail-closed. options are per tool and only the documented names are accepted - call get_table_native_tools for the current list. Owner email finder needs an owner first name plus the company website; point options.owner_name_column at an Owner name finder column to source the name, which auto_run requires. Business email finder is a SEPARATE column - create it with its own call and set options.owner_email_column to run it behind an owner finder. Business email finder also has careful options for a Table that runs by itself. confirmed_only keeps an address only when the email check says it is real (verified, or an exact Role answer), tries the next name only when this mailbox does not exist, never keeps a catch all, unknown or full mailbox answer, and saves each answer the way a Verify email column does, so that column gets it for free afterwards. require_mail_server skips a website with no mail server at no charge. max_checks keeps a row to 1, 2 or 3 names. skip_shared_website skips, at no charge, a website that is a shared page or that another lead of the workspace also has. write_to_lead_email writes a confirmed address on a lead that has no email yet, and never an address another lead already has. run_if runs a row only when a condition is true. A Table under a search plan's limits only takes this finder with confirmed_only on. new_rows_only (with auto_run) runs only rows added from now on: rows already in the Table are not run, nothing is queued or held, and no confirmation is needed. The Catch-all verifier is NOT creatable here: it needs a Verify email column that has already RUN and returned Catch All or Unknown, so use verify_catchall per address, or add the column from the Table's add-column menu. Retry contract: Durable Idempotency-Key required. Transient retries replay one stored result.

Leave confirm_auto_run and confirmed_credits out. Use this on a Table that already has many rows, such as the first Table of a search plan. Every cell must include value; explicit null clears it. Formats: text is at most 10,000 characters, number/currency is a finite number, checkbox is boolean, date is YYYY-MM-DD, email is valid and at most 320 characters, URL is absolute HTTP(S) and at most 2,048 characters, select is one configured token, and multi_select is a unique token array of at most 100 values. The whole request is validated before writing. Returns updated and skipped counts, and triggers configured row_updated rules once per changed lead. The write itself does not run enrichment or charge Scrapeloop credits. Retry contract: Proven idempotent write. Retries transient failures with bounded backoff.

value.description: Required. Pass null explicitly to clear the cell.

tools.name: import_leads
tools.description: Bring your own leads: atomically import externally-sourced records into a campaign-bindable Scrapeloop Table without scraping or lead credits. A generic record needs at least one of: email, linkedin_url, external_id (your own id for the record) or an absolute source_url (the page the record came from), so Scrapeloop can tell which lead it is. Email may be null. Records from a public source list cannot be imported here, only previewed. The rules for such records (sourcing_contract) switch on when you pass sourcing_contract:true, and also by themselves when one record carries source, source_state and niche together. A real import is then refused with 409 and nothing is imported: no lead, no Table. The 409 has an error sentence written for the user (it says what was seen, such as how many records carry all three, and what to change: show it as it is written), destination "agency_local_businesses" and dry_run_available:true. Use preview_import to see what such records would do. That preview has a warning that says the same. A reason of a skipped record there ends with: fixing this will not get it imported. Follow the warning, do not try to make such records pass. In that preview each record needs a controlled source, source_state and niche and a valid phone or email, a local business with only a phone gets an id made from its source and its phone, and source and niche tags are worked out. If these are the user's own leads, say what happened and ask before you change them: without source_state the same records import as ordinary leads. Matching is workspace-scoped and deterministic: normalized email first, then local-business phone, canonical LinkedIn, then external_id or source_url. The legacy dedupe_by="external_id" mode matches by external_id or source_url first. A later record with a real email merges into the earlier lead that only had a LinkedIn link, an external_id or a source_url, instead of duplicating it. No placeholder emails are created. verification_status and custom_fields are preserved, and custom_fields flow to Instantly as custom variables. Target list_id or pass list_name to create-or-get a Table. Batch up to 1000 records. One operation_id is reused across HTTP retries, so an uncertain response can be recovered without duplicating leads. You may pass a prior operation_id; reusing it with different inputs returns 409. Each record: {source?, source_state?, email?, linkedin_url?, source_url?, external_id?, first_name, last_name, business_name, phone, website, address, city, state_region, country, niche, rating, reviews_count, gbp_link?, facebook?, instagram?, verification_status ("verified"|"catchall_verified"|"unverified"|"risky"|"invalid"), strategy_tags:[], custom_fields:{}}. Returns {operation_id, list_id, inserted, updated, deduped, invalid, invalid_reasons}. Each entry of invalid_reasons has a reason written for the user: show it as it is written. A lead keeps the marks no_resale, workspace_only and legal_basis gdpr_li (extra fields that say the lead needs more care) once it has them: a later import cannot turn them off. When the answer has marks_kept_note, show it as it is written. Retry contract: Proven idempotent write. Retries transient failures with bounded backoff.

operation_id.description: Optional retry key from a prior ambiguous call.

dedupe_by.description: "email" (default, with LinkedIn/source fallbacks) or legacy "external_id" priority

tools.description: List the APPROVED Apify actors you may run/import from. Arbitrary Apify actors are NOT allowed: only vetted actors (website content, contact info with add-ons off, google search with add-ons off) can be used, and LinkedIn / Facebook-group / social-graph actors are always rejected. Returns [{actor_id, add_ons_allowed}]. Use this before preview_apify_import to pick a permitted actor_id. Retry contract: Read-only operation. Retries transport errors, 429, and 5xx with bounded backoff.

tools.name: preview_apify_import
tools.description: Read-only preview of an approved Apify actor's already-produced dataset before importing it. mapping is {lead_field: dotted.source.path} where lead_field is one of name, email, phone, domain, organization_name, city, state, country, linkedin_url, title. Normalizes the whole dataset (rows with no email/phone/domain/linkedin/name are skipped), returns the first 25 rows plus record_count (the true total) and a preview_hash. Pass that preview_hash to import_apify_dataset: the import re-verifies it and refuses (409) if the dataset changed. Does NOT run the actor or spend: it reads an existing dataset_id. Returns {dataset_id, actor_id, record_count, preview, preview_truncated, preview_hash}. Retry contract: Read-only operation. Retries transport errors, 429, and 5xx with bounded backoff.

dataset_id.description: Apify dataset id from a completed actor run.

tools.name: import_apify_dataset
tools.description: Import a previewed Apify dataset (≤1000 rows) into a private Scrapeloop Table through the bring-your-own-leads funnel (dedupe + identity matching + Table attach reused; no lead credits). Call preview_apify_import first and pass its preview_hash: the import re-reads the dataset and returns 409 (preview_drift) if it changed since preview. Each row gets a stable external_id (apify:{dataset}:{row}) so re-importing updates rather than duplicates; company lands in business_name and the contact name/title ride through as custom fields. Target list_id, or omit for a new "Apify import" Table. Returns the import funnel result {inserted, updated, deduped, invalid, ...}. Retry contract: Proven idempotent write. Retries transient failures with bounded backoff.

tools.name: capture_community_intent
tools.description: Manually record one reviewed, high-intent public community signal or admin-approved opt-in. This is not a social scraper. Private content, group member lists, membership-only evidence, reactions, follows, automated messages, cookies, and platform-control bypasses are prohibited. Required evidence is minimized to policy basis, visibility, consent mode, source and public-profile URLs, observed timestamp, evidence class, company, and reviewer note. Pending signals default to outreach_ready=false and legal_review_required=true. A business email is accepted only after approval and only when it was published for business contact or explicitly opted in. Set dry_run=true first. The mutation is idempotent through operation_id and writes reviewer lineage before any Table import. Retry contract: Proven idempotent write. Retries transient failures with bounded backoff.

tools.name: import_leads_csv
tools.description: Bring your own leads from CSV/TSV into a campaign-bindable Table. Each row needs at least one of: email, LinkedIn URL, external ID or an absolute source URL, so Scrapeloop can tell which lead it is. A row with no email needs no placeholder email. The parser auto-detects the delimiter, maps common headers (including linkedin_url and source_url), preserves unmapped columns as custom_fields, and normalizes verifier verdicts. A CSV from a public source list cannot be imported here, only previewed. A file with source, source_state and niche columns switches on the rules for such lists (sourcing_contract) by itself, and so does sourcing_contract:true. A real import of it is refused with 409 and nothing is imported: no lead, no Table. The 409 has an error sentence written for the user (it says what was seen, such as the names of the three columns, and what to change: show it as it is written), destination "agency_local_businesses" and dry_run_available:true. With dry_run:true the same file is previewed (the answer then has a warning that says the real import will be refused, and what to change): every loaded row must also have a valid phone or email, source IDs are namespaced, a local business with only a phone gets an id made from its source and its phone, and source/niche tags are worked out. If this is the user's own file, say what happened and ask before you change it: without the source_state column the same rows import as ordinary leads. With a name of its own, such as Lead state, that column is kept as an extra field. Matching is workspace-scoped: email first, then local-business phone, LinkedIn, then external ID or source URL. Set dry_run:true first to preview writes and column mapping. Mutating CSV imports are atomic and reuse one operation_id across HTTP retries. You may pass a prior operation_id; reusing it with changed CSV inputs returns 409. No scraping, lead credits, or re-verification. Target list_id or pass list_name. Up to 1000 rows per call. Skipped rows come back in invalid_reasons. Each entry has a reason written for the user: show it as it is written. A lead keeps the marks no_resale, workspace_only and legal_basis gdpr_li (extra fields that say the lead needs more care) once it has them: a later import cannot turn them off. When the answer has marks_kept_note, show it as it is written. Retry contract: Proven idempotent write. Retries transient failures with bounded backoff.

tools.name: create_table_flow_rule
tools.description: Create a Table automation rule. Conditions use FilterExpr. Actions route one matching row to another Table, a campaign, or a public webhook. Retry contract: One request only. An ambiguous result returns reconciliation tools and stable match fields.

tools.name: toggle_table_flow_rule
tools.description: Enable or disable one saved Table automation rule. Retry contract: Proven idempotent write. Retries transient failures with bounded backoff.

tools.name: update_table_flow_rule
tools.description: Change one saved Table rule in place: its condition, name, action settings, daily limit or delay. Send only what changes. A condition replaces the whole saved condition, so start from the one list_table_flow_rules returns (or from a fix that check_campaign_setup names) and keep every "not in that Table" guard. The rule keeps its id, history and counters. On a Table that belongs to a running complete plan, pause the plan first: a changed rule needs a fresh review and launch. Use toggle_table_flow_rule to switch a rule on or off. Retry contract: Proven idempotent write. Retries transient failures with bounded backoff.

tools.name: run_table_flow_rule_for_waiting_rows
tools.description: Run one saved Table rule for the rows that meet it right now and have not moved. A rule only runs when something happens to a lead, so leads can meet a rule and stay where they are: the rule was changed after they arrived, or a check finished and no rule looked again. check_campaign_setup names this tool under "Leads meet a rule and have not moved". It only works for a rule that sends leads to another Table, that is switched on and not paused, on a normal Table of 5,000 rows or fewer. A rule that asks for a saved review count only on a Table of 100 rows or fewer. With dry_run true (the default) it only reads. It returns count (the leads that meet the rule now, have not gone on and have nothing waiting to handle them), would_queue, sends_to (where the rule sends them, with the paid checks that Table runs on new leads by itself and the credits a lead), plan (the search plan these Tables belong to), and a title and lines ready to show the person. To run it, call it again with dry_run false and expected_count set to that count. If the count changed in between, nothing is put in line and the new count comes back: show a fresh dry run. A real run moves nothing itself. It puts the leads in line for this one rule, at most 1,000 a call (left_waiting says how many are left, so call again when those are handled). The rule then looks at each lead again when its turn comes, about 2 seconds a lead, so a lead that no longer meets the rule stays where it is. The loop guard and the daily limit of the rule apply as always, and a rule with a wait keeps its wait. Always show the dry run lines first and run only after the person says yes: a lead that moves on can start a paid check in the next Table. On a Table of a running search plan the plan starts no new search until these leads are handled, and this tool never pauses or starts a plan. Under a hard monthly limit the campaign only takes leads that the searches of that plan found, so never promise that a moved lead goes into the campaign. One operation_id is reused across retries, so a lost reply never puts a lead in line twice. Retry contract: Proven idempotent write. Retries transient failures with bounded backoff.

list_id.description: The Table the rule is on.

dry_run.description: True (the default) only reads. Only a real false runs the rule.

expected_count.description: The count of the dry run the person was shown. Needed with dry_run false.

tools.name: preview_table_write_back
tools.description: FREE dry-run of writing a column's settled values onto the leads' real field (one of: email, phone, domain, name, city, state, country, postal_code, address_line1). Returns fill-empty / conflicts / duplicates / invalid counts. ALWAYS run this and show the counts before apply_table_write_back. A verify column is refused (it already writes email_status). Retry contract: Read-only operation. Retries transport errors, 429, and 5xx with bounded backoff.

tools.name: apply_table_write_back
tools.description: Write a column's settled cell values onto the leads' real field. Fill-empty by default; set overwrite=true to replace a DIFFERENT existing value. FREE (writes lead fields, spends nothing). A changed email resets email_status to 'unverified' unless the cell proves that exact address was verified; a known-invalid email is never written even with overwrite. Run preview_table_write_back and confirm with the user first. Retry contract: Proven idempotent write. Retries transient failures with bounded backoff.

tools.description: Export a table to CSV as a background job. scope is the same view/filter/selection object used by table runs; fields are ordered lead.<field>/col.<column_key> keys and default to what the view shows. Returns job_id; poll get_table_export for a download link valid for 7 days. Retry contract: One request only. An ambiguous result returns reconciliation tools and stable match fields.

tools.name: get_table_export
tools.description: Get one table export and its signed download URL, or omit job_id to list recent background exports. Retry contract: Read-only operation. Retries transport errors, 429, and 5xx with bounded backoff.

tools.name: list_table_rows
tools.description: Read a table's rows the way the grid sees them: lead identity fields (name/email/phone/domain/city/state/country/status) plus every column's cell (status + value). Server-side: sort is a JSON-array string like [{"key":"lead.name","dir":"asc"},{"key":"col.company_size","dir":"desc"}] (keys are lead.<field> or col.<column_key>, ≤3 levels); q is a full-text search across identity fields + visible column cells; filter is a FilterExpr object (same grammar the Tables filter UI uses), e.g. {"and":[{"field":"lead.email_status","op":"eq","value":"valid"},{"field":"col.company_size","op":"gte","value":50}]}, and adds total_filtered alongside total; pass the previous response's next_cursor back as cursor to page (null next_cursor = last page). Distinct from get_list_rows (the plain import read-back). limit ≤ 500. Retry contract: Read-only operation. Retries transport errors, 429, and 5xx with bounded backoff.

filter.description: FilterExpr JSON (object): server-side row filter; adds total_filtered. lead.email_domain derives the exact lowercase domain from the current email, separate from website lead.domain. lead.gcid reads an exact Google category ID from current source data; it does not prove business fit. Use eq/any_of/none_of for exact lists; add not_empty to hold missing or malformed values. No DNS or provider lookup. lead.email_check is the exact saved email check result for the current address (safe, role, catch_all, disposable, inbox_full, disabled, invalid, unknown), empty when never checked; lead.email_status risky holds both role and inbox_full, so use lead.email_check any_of ["safe","role"] for an exact rule.

Pass a returned id (or a system key) as view_id to list_table_rows to read that view (a saved filter + sorts + column overlay). Retry contract: Read-only operation. Retries transport errors, 429, and 5xx with bounded backoff.

tools.name: create_table_view
tools.description: Save a custom view of an active table: a named filter (FilterExpr) + sorts + column overlay + row window (all optional beyond name). filter_expression uses the same grammar as list_table_rows; sorts is [{key,dir}]. The create is retry-safe: one operation_id is reused across HTTP retries. You may pass a prior operation_id to recover an ambiguous call; reusing it with different inputs returns 409. Retry contract: Proven idempotent write. Retries transient failures with bounded backoff.

operation_id.description: Optional retry key from a prior ambiguous call.

tools.name: update_table_view
tools.description: Update a saved table view: any field (name/description/filter_expression/sorts/column_state/row_window); a field set to null clears it. tools.name: estimate_table_column
tools.description: FREE cost preview for running one enrichment column, optionally scoped to a view or selection (view_id + selection{mode:'query', filter:<FilterExpr>, exclude_ids} or {mode:'explicit', ids}). cell_filter picks which cells: 'empty_or_stale' (default in the UI; skips results still fresh under the current column config), 'failed', or 'all'; n_rows/start_row window the run (1-based). Returns lead_count + estimated_cost_usd + scope_resolved. ALWAYS show this to the user before run_table_column; it spends nothing. Retry contract: Read-only operation. Retries transport errors, 429, and 5xx with bounded backoff.

Run estimate_table_column first and confirm with the user. Retry contract: Never retried automatically. An ambiguous result must be reconciled before any new attempt.

tools.name: run_scope_summary
tools.description: FREE counts + estimates for a column run scope: total, empty_or_stale, stale, failed rows + est_all/est_empty_or_stale/est_first_10 USD + budget. Use to decide what to run (which cell_filter) before estimate/run_table_column. Read-only. Retry contract: Read-only operation. Retries transport errors, 429, and 5xx with bounded backoff.

tools.name: estimate_table_run_all
tools.description: FREE per-column preview + total for running EVERY enrichment column in dependency order, optionally scoped (view_id + selection). Show before run_table_all; spends nothing. Retry contract: Read-only operation. Retries transport errors, 429, and 5xx with bounded backoff.

Run estimate_table_run_all first and confirm with the user. Retry contract: Never retried automatically. An ambiguous result must be reconciled before any new attempt.
